profiles.name: Sylver Pondolfino
profiles.description:
Sylver Pondolfino is an activist documented in Nuclear Resister’s reporting on protest arrests.

On 2025-04-16, Sylver Pondolfino was arrested at Creech Air Force Base, Nevada. Cited during the Sacred Peace Walk roadway blockade. A May 28 court appearance was specified; no jail term is established.

On 2024-03-27, Sylver Pondolfino was arrested at Creech Air Force Base / Clark County Jail, Nevada. Arrested during a roadway blockade, taken to Clark County Jail in Las Vegas and later released. The report does not give the release date or a numerical custody duration.
profiles.finding: Named single-subject portrait in States of Incarceration Collateral Damage, credited Nicholai Kellman. NYC/Picture the Homeless biography matches public professional biography; Nuclear Resister identifies Staten Island activist. Original1200x960 verified and deployed.

profiles.name: Tarek Bazrouk
profiles.description: Tarek Bazrouk was a young Palestinian-American student active in New York City demonstrations concerning Israel’s war in Gaza. Federal prosecutors charged him with hate crimes for assaults on three Jewish or pro-Israel counter-demonstrators at protests in April and December 2024 and January 2025. Bazrouk pleaded guilty in June 2025, acknowledging that he selected the victims because of their Jewish religion or Israeli national origin. He had been held without release since his May 7, 2025 arrest. On October 28, 2025, U.S. District Judge Richard Berman sentenced him to seventeen months in prison followed by three years of supervised release. Palestine-solidarity organizations argued that federal intervention in matters already proceeding in state court reflected selective and politically escalated prosecution; more than 12,000 people supported a request for time served. Bazrouk was released on June 23, 2026 after 413 days in custody and completion of an early-release program.
profiles.finding: JTA/Jerusalem Post identifies action image credited SDNY; Free Tarek campaign Linktree has possible portrait/zine leads. Individual image inspection outstanding.

profiles.name: Gregory Vandenberg
profiles.description: Gregory Vandenberg is a former U.S. Navy SEAL who was arrested while traveling toward the June 2025 No Kings protest in San Diego. Prosecutors said he bought mortar fireworks and firecrackers in New Mexico and intended to use them against police at the demonstration. A federal jury convicted him in January 2026 of transporting explosives with intent to kill, injure, or intimidate and attempting to transport prohibited fireworks into California. He was sentenced to sixteen months in federal prison.
profiles.finding: NavyNews reproduces named store surveillance frame; AP case corroborated. Not yet inspected for usable facial detail. Unrelated crash researcher/student newspaper namesakes not accepted.

profiles.name: Brendan Munro Thompson
profiles.description: Brendan Munro Thompson, publicly identified as Bella Thompson and Bella Castillo, was arrested after an immigration protest near Coast Guard Island in Alameda on October 23, 2025. Federal officers shot Thompson after prosecutors alleged that a rented truck was reversed toward their blockade. Thompson was treated for the gunshot wound, held for a psychiatric evaluation, booked into Santa Rita Jail, and charged federally. A judge released Thompson on bail on November 21, 2025 to live with family and attend outpatient mental-health treatment while the case continued.
profiles.finding: DOJ complaint confirms Bella Thompson/Castillo aliases. KQED bail report lead is courthouse, not portrait. Actress and Mississippi student namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Russell Gomez Dzul
profiles.description: Russell Gomez Dzul was stopped by Border Patrol while riding a bicycle in Los Angeles County on June 7, 2025 during the federal immigration operations that prompted widespread protests. Agents arrested him and accused him of kicking an officer while handcuffed in a patrol vehicle. Prosecutors reduced the original felony allegation to a misdemeanor. A jury acquitted Gomez Dzul on January 14, 2026, but he remained in ICE custody because of his immigration status.
profiles.finding: LA Public Press and NACDL court filing corroborate cyclist case; no individually verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Emily Gabriella Sommer
profiles.description: Emily Gabriella Sommer was prosecuted after spitting on interim U.S. Attorney Ed Martin during a May 8, 2025 sidewalk interview and assaulting two deputy U.S. marshals during her May 22 arrest. She was initially released, then jailed after a June 9 arrest and alleged release-condition violations. Sommer pleaded guilty to three counts of assaulting government officials and was sentenced on October 10, 2025 to time served after roughly four months in the D.C. jail, followed by one year of supervised release.
profiles.finding: DOJ affidavit explicitly includes booking photo. Requires PDF image extraction and quality check, carried forward.

profiles.name: George Killingsworth
profiles.description: George Killingsworth is a retired pastor and longtime peace activist. On March 27, 2024, during an anti-drone protest outside Creech Air Force Base in Nevada, he was arrested after drawing a chalk peace sign on a large boulder near the gate. He was charged with defacing public property and released outside the base the same day. The available account does not document booking into jail or any period of confinement.
profiles.finding: Berkeley/Creech activist established in Nuclear Resister; Cook County arrest and LOC veteran matches not linked. No verified portrait.

profiles.name: Csaba John Csukas
profiles.description: Csaba John Csukas, 39, of Daly City CA, naturalized US citizen who arrived as a refugee of the Bosnian war, was arrested October 26, 2023 at SFO for allegedly hitting a rideshare customer in the face after asking if he was Jewish or Israeli. Indicted March 12, 2024 on federal hate-crime charges. Acquitted - jury found insufficient evidence of religious or national bias motivation.
profiles.finding: Exact-name Medium/LinkedIn photo lead exists but no independent link to SFO defendant established. Telex case report corroborates name; identity verification remains open.

profiles.name: Zayneabideen Rasul Al-Murshidi
profiles.description: Zayneabideen Rasul Al-Murshidi joined a March 11, 2024 Palestine-solidarity action that blocked Interstate 95 near Richmond. Nine demonstrators linked themselves with ladders, chains, and “sleeping dragon” devices to demand an end to United States support for Israel’s war in Gaza. Virginia State Police arrested the group. On June 24, Richmond General District Court Judge Mansi Shah imposed a jail sentence for stopping traffic; Zayneabideen Rasul Al-Murshidi received five days in jail.
profiles.finding: Exact full-name Richmond query located shared local case coverage; no individually captioned portrait identified.

profiles.name: Hicham Talal
profiles.description: Hicham Talal, 24, was arrested February 26, 2024 for vandalizing a Webster Bank in West Hartford CT for its investments in Israeli weapons manufacturing. Charged with hate-crime-enhanced criminal mischief; charges dropped July 29, 2024 after public protest pressure.
profiles.finding: CT Insider/NR case reports located. West Haven LinkedIn identity not independently tied to defendant; Moroccan namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Muhammad Pahlawan
profiles.description:
Muhammad Pahlawan is a Pakistani national convicted in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia of transporting Iranian-made advanced conventional weaponry bound for Yemen's Houthi movement. On January 11, 2024, U.S. Central Command naval forces operating from the USS Lewis B. Puller — including Navy SEALs and a U.S. Coast Guard Maritime Security Response Team — boarded the unflagged dhow Pahlawan captained in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Somalia and seized ballistic-missile components, anti-ship cruise-missile components, and a warhead. Two Navy SEALs, Christopher Chambers and Nathan Gage Ingram, were lost at sea during the interdiction.

On June 5, 2025, a federal jury convicted Pahlawan of conspiring to provide and providing material support to terrorists, providing material support to Iran's and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' weapons-of-mass-destruction programs, conspiring to and transporting explosive devices to the Houthis knowing they would be used to cause harm, and threatening his crew. On October 16, 2025, U.S. District Judge David J. Novak sentenced him to 40 years in prison.
profiles.finding: DOJ/IranWatch complaint and AP case reports located; ship/military images not portraits. Medieval ruler namesake excluded.

profiles.name: Karrem Nasr
profiles.description: Karrem Nasr, 23, of New Jersey, was charged in late December 2023 by SDNY with attempting to join and provide material support to al-Shabaab, a designated FTO. Cited the October 7, 2023 attack as motivation. Pleaded guilty; sentenced to 60 months federal prison + 15 years supervised release.
profiles.finding: ABC named-image search result needs caution: source credit Getty and contextual caption do not themselves prove portrait. Original visual inspection remains open; DOJ complaint corroborates case.

profiles.name: Terrence Clyne
profiles.description: Terrence Clyne, 68, of Orland Park IL, was charged with misdemeanor battery and felony hate crime for punching his Palestinian neighbor while shouting hateful remarks; dispute stemmed from trash can placement in shared driveway. Pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery; felony hate crime dropped. Probation.
profiles.finding: Patch named photo matches age68, Orland Park, neighbor case. Police credit retained. Nashville obituary78-year-old namesake rejected. Original613x460 verified and deployed.

profiles.name: Kyra Hanlon
profiles.description: Activist arrested December 22, 2023 during a "Forest Friday" weekly picket outside the Atlanta Public Safety Training Center ("Cop City") construction site in Weelaunee forest (South River Forest). She was one of three people collectively known as the "Weelaunee Three" charged with criminal trespass and held overnight in DeKalb County Jail before being released on December 23, 2023. In March 2025 prosecutors offered all three pretrial diversion requiring a rehabilitation course in exchange for dropping the charges.
profiles.finding: Atlanta Press Collective names Weelaunee Three in group photo. Georgetown author headshot and Inquirer wedding profile are unlinked leads, not accepted without identity corroboration.
